`Compliance.CompliedWith` demanded § 107.51's limitations out of the section's order, by swapping the first two `Demands.Of` calls after the gate so the groundspeed was demanded before the bound person (`var speed = Demands.Of(groundspeed, ...); var asked = Demands.Of(person, ...);` for the other way round). The gate still came first, so nothing about a waived request moved -- which is the point: this test pins the OTHER half of `docs/decisions/0008-the-waiver-gate-precedes-every-other-demand.md`, that what moved was the gate's position and not what a reachable entry demands. A caller stating that no waiver of § 107.51 is in force and describing nothing else was refused naming `Groundspeed` where the entry owes `Person` first. This test went red on both target frameworks: `Failed!  - Failed:     2, Passed:   741, Skipped:     0, Total:   743` for net10.0 and the same figures for net8.0, on `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ`, `Expected: "Person"` against `Actual: "Groundspeed"`, together with `OperatingLimitationsEntryPointTests.The_dictionary_dispatch_refuses_rather_than_answering_from_defaults`. The fifteen handler mutations recorded above cannot redden this test by construction -- re-wrapping an input in `Demand(...)` throws the same `ArgumentException` with the same `ParamName` on the no-waiver path -- which is why it has a mutation of its own.
